neighbours.label: the determiner of an object taken up in a reply or concession: verbs of returning, conceding, acceding to, denying or refusing ('return the favour', 'concede the point', 'denies this'), as against ordinary transactional verbs (buy, approve, paint) with the same determiners
fire: He waved from across the street, and she was quick to return the greeting.
After a long silence, the professor had to concede the argument to his student.
The landlord eventually agreed to this demand and lowered the rent.
The company strongly denies this and says the figures are wrong.
My brother refused to give up the secret no matter how often we asked.
She raised her glass and he gladly returned the toast.
The general reluctantly conceded this point during the inquiry.
When the reporter asked about the leak, the spokesman rejected the claim outright.
quiet: He waved from across the street, and she was quick to cross the road.
After a long silence, the professor had to clean the board for his student.
The landlord eventually painted this hallway and fixed the lights.
The company strongly prefers this supplier and orders from them weekly.
My brother refused to eat the soup no matter how often we asked.
She raised her glass and he gladly filled the jug.
The general reluctantly signed this form during the visit.
When the reporter arrived at the office, the spokesman carried the boxes outside.
